newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate seesaws, ends up on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate seesaws, ends up on speculation.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed up 50 basis points at 30.00 percent on Thursday after zizagging throughout the session on speculation, traders said.
"The market was speculative again, with rates varying between 50 basis points up and down from yesterday's close," said a trader.
"Short term paper was only in demand to cover specific needs, but term paper was in a little more demand," he added.
Traders said that the 1997 budget proposals presented to congress at midsession had little impact as they were in line with expectations.
Among other forecasts, the government expected growth for next year to be four percent, and for the peso to trade at an average of 8.53 per dollar.
"The market is still quite listless. Even though the peso recovered a little, some are still trying to play around with rates," said another dealer.
"Inflation figures were good, however, so I would hope that pressure on rates dies down tomorrow," he added.
Banco de Mexico said consumer inflation for October was 1.25 percent for October, or slightly below average expectations of 1.30 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 25 basis points at 31.25 percent.
Banco de Mexico injected 2.301 billion pesos into the secondary market by auctioning two credits at 32.06 and 31.80 percent.
Total credit maturities for Friday were estimated at 8.866 billion pesos.
